invariantAllocations.invariant: Program Kit-owned C# implementation satisfies the current private repository source-quality policy.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing private Program Kit source gate already applies to the CLI, serializers, filesystem mechanics, and tests changed by this design.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Each supported provider adapter renders only to its exact reviewed project-scoped discovery root.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Provider discovery roots, filesystem containment, and external provider behavior require byte-level fixtures and clean-session evidence.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Every Program Kit-owned provider wrapper remains represented by exact ownership evidence until explicit exact-byte removal.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Lock serialization, migration, collision handling, transactions, and filesystem bytes cannot be proven by a source analyzer.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Program Kit never selects a consumer integration posture, changes ignore rules, stages files, commits files, grants provider authority, or starts work.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Source dependency checks, command fixtures, documentation conformance, and human review prove the absence of forbidden integration behavior.

rationale: The existing private Program Kit C# gate is compatible with Program Kit-owned implementation. Provider discovery, multi-provider ownership, migration, removal, Git posture, documentation, and clean-session behavior remain exact executable and human-review obligations. No new analyzer, gate extension, or consumer attachment is justified.
residualRisks: The private Program Kit gate remains a repository-specific MSBuild trust boundary.
Static analysis cannot prove provider discovery, filesystem transactions, exact Git posture, user-global absence, clean-session loading, or external provider behavior.
Official provider discovery contracts can change after design approval and therefore require implementation-time freshness checks.
nonStaticClaims: Exact bundle verification, provider allow-listing, lock migration, collision handling, transactional update, exact removal, cancellation, clean-clone behavior, and unrelated-byte preservation require dedicated executable tests.
Consumer README clarity, selective Git tracking, and genuine provider discovery remain documentation and human-review obligations.
No runtime package or generated application loads capability prose or provider configuration.
